translations.text: The Wisdom of Ben Sira
All wisdom comes from the Lord, and she has been with him from eternity.
Who can count the sand of the sea, the drops of rain, and the days of eternity?
Who can measure the height of heaven, the breadth of the earth, and the great deep?
Wisdom surpasses all these, and faithfulness has been strong from the earliest times.
To whom have the roots of wisdom been revealed, and who knows the hidden depths of understanding?
There is one who alone is awesome: God, who rules over all her treasures.
He examined her, saw her, counted her, gave her, and distributed her among all his works.
He gave her to all flesh as he wished, and bestowed her abundantly on all who fear him.
The fear of the Lord is splendor, honor, greatness, and a crown of praise.
The fear of the Lord gladdens the heart, bringing joy, delight, and eternal life.
Whoever fears God will have a good end and will be blessed at the end of his days.
The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and she was created with the faithful in their mothers’ wombs.
She is with truthful people, and she was established from eternity; her kindness endures with their offspring.
The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and she satisfies with happiness from the abundance of her produce.
Wisdom fills all her storehouses and treasuries with her produce.
The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and she increases peace, life, and healing.
She is a strong staff and a support, everlasting praise and honor for everyone who follows her.
And when you approach, be like a warrior and a mighty man.
My son, do not be false in your fear of the Lord, and do not approach it with a divided heart.
Do not use it to seek honor in the eyes of others, and be very careful with your lips.

Do not hate her teaching or waver, and do not heap disgrace on yourself, lest the Lord increase your bonds and cast you down in the assembly, because you have claimed to fear God while the inside of your heart is full of deceit.
My son, if you have approached the fear of God, you have handed yourself over to every kind of trial.
Cling to it and do not let it go, so that you may become wise in your ways.
Accept everything that comes upon you, and be patient in sickness and poverty.
For gold is tested in fire, and a human being in the furnace of poverty.
Trust in God, and he will be your helper. Hope in him, and he will make your paths straight.
You who fear the Lord, hope for his goodness, and do not fall behind him, lest you fall.
You who fear the Lord, trust in him, and he will not delay your reward.
You who fear the Lord, hope for his goodness, for everlasting joy and salvation.

Consider what happened in former times; reflect on the generations of old and see: who trusted in him and was abandoned by him? Who relied on him and was cast aside? Who called on him and received no answer?
For the Lord is gracious and compassionate. He hears and saves in every time of distress, and he listens to the voice of those who do his will.
A faint heart and weak hands, a person who walks along many paths.
Woe to the heart that does not trust! It too will not stand firm.
Woe to you, mighty men of confidence! What will you do when the Lord judges?
Those who fear the Lord will not reject his word, and those who love him will keep his ways.
Those who fear the Lord will seek his will, and those who love him will learn his law.
Whoever fears God will prepare his heart, but whoever abandons him destroys his own soul.
For his mercy is as great as his greatness, and his deeds match his name.
Children, listen to your fathers and act accordingly, so that you may live forever and ever.
For the Lord has honored the father above his children and confirmed a mother's authority over her children.
Whoever honors his father will have his sins forgiven.
Whoever honors his mother stores up treasures.
Whoever honors his father will rejoice in his son, and when he prays, he will be heard and answered.
Whoever honors his father will have a long life, and whoever honors his mother lays good [?] upon God.
My son, honor your father in deed and word, so that all his blessings may come upon you.
A father's blessing establishes dwellings, but a mother's curse uproots their foundations.
Do not seek honor through your father's disgrace, for it brings you no honor.
For a man's honor is his father's honor, and whoever dishonors his mother incurs great sins.
My son, be steadfast in honoring your father, and do not cease to honor him all the days of your life.
Even if his understanding fails, bear with him, and do not shame him all the days of his life.
Kindness to a father is not forgotten; it is set against sins.
On the day of distress it will be remembered in your favor, like heat upon ice, to wipe away your sins.
For whoever despises his father blasphemes, and whoever dishonors his mother is cursed before his Creator.
My son, conduct yourself humbly in your wealth, and you will be loved more than a man who gives gifts.
In everything that is great in the world, make yourself small, and you will find mercy before God.
For God's mercies are many, and mysteries are revealed to the humble.
Do not seek things too difficult for you, and do not investigate things beyond your strength.
Consider what has been entrusted to you, and do not rely on hidden things.
Do not occupy yourself with the rest of his works, for things beyond you have been shown to you.
For human thoughts are many, and evil imaginings lead people astray.
Someone whose eyes have no pupils lacks light. When you are blind to knowledge, do not offer advice to persuade others.
A hard heart will come to a bad end, and whoever loves good things will walk in them.
A hard heart will have many pains, and an insolent person will add sins to sins.
There is no healing for the wound of a scoffer, for he is a plant from an evil stock.
A wise heart will understand the sayings of the wise, and a listening ear will rejoice in the wise.
Water extinguishes a blazing fire; likewise, giving to the poor brings forgiveness of sins.
Whoever does good is prepared for his journey, and when he falls, he finds support.
My son, do not mock the life of a poor person, and do not strike a poor person in distress.
Do not wound the spirit of someone in need, and do not lead the spirit of a broken person astray.
Do not cause pain to a poor person's stomach, and do not withhold a gift from someone in need.
Do not disregard a poor person's plea.
And do not give him cause to curse you.
For the one whose mouth is bitter curses with all his soul, and his Creator hears the sound of his cry.
Make yourself loved by the congregation, and bow your head before the rulers of the city.
Incline your ear to the poor person, and answer him peaceably and humbly.
Rescue the oppressed person from his oppressors, and do not lose heart in giving a just judgment.
Be like a father to orphans and take the place of a husband to widows, and you will be like a son to God, and he will have mercy on you.
Wisdom has taught her children and will enlighten all who understand her.
Those who love her love life, and those who seek her will receive favor from the Lord.
Those who cling to her will find honor before God, and the place the Lord has blessed will be their dwelling.
Those who serve her serve the sanctuary, and God loves her dwelling place.
Whoever listens to me will judge truthfully, and whoever pays attention to me will dwell within me.
If he believes in me, he will inherit me and receive me for all generations forever.
For I will walk with him along winding paths and test him first. I will bring fear and trembling upon him and examine him through my trials until his heart has full confidence in me.
I will turn back and set things right with him, and reveal all my secrets to him.
But if he turns away from following me, I will cast him aside and hand him over to plunderers.
Watch for the right time, beware of evil, and do not be ashamed of yourself.
For there is shame that produces sins, and there is shame whose honor is grace.
Do not show partiality to yourself, and do not be ashamed to admit your failings.
Do not withhold a word at its proper time, and do not hide your wisdom.
For wisdom is made known through speech, and understanding through what the tongue says.
Do not deny the truth, and refrain from your foolish acts.
Do not be ashamed to confess your sins, and do not stand against a fool.
Do not bow yourself down to a fool, and do not quarrel with a ruler.
Fight for the truth until death, and the Lord will fight for you.
Do not be boastful with your tongue but slack and sluggish in your deeds.
Do not be a dog in your house, or angry and frightening in your dealings.
Do not have your hand stretched out to receive but closed when it comes to giving.
Do not rely on your possessions and say, “I have plenty.”
Do not rely on your strength to follow the desires of your heart.
Do not say, “Who can match my strength?” For the Lord avenges all who are oppressed.
Do not say, “I sinned, and nothing happened to me,” for God is patient.
Do not rely on forgiveness, lest you add sins to sins.
For mercy and wrath are with him, and his wrath will rest upon the wicked.
Do not delay returning to him, and do not put it off from day to day, for wrath comes suddenly, and destruction comes at the time of repayment.
Do not rely on unjustly gained wealth, for it will not help you on the day of distress.
Do not be driven along by every wind or turn down every path.
Be firm in your judgment, and let your word remain consistent.
Be quick to listen, and take your time in giving an answer.
If you have something to say, answer your neighbor; otherwise, put your hand over your mouth.
Honor and disgrace are in the hands of the speaker, and people's tongues bring them down.
Do not be called two-faced, and do not stumble with your tongue, for shame was made for the thief, and grievous disgrace for someone who is two-faced.
Do no wrong in matters great or small.
Do not become an enemy instead of a friend, lest you inherit a bad name and disgrace. Reproach and guilt fall on someone who is two-faced.
Do not surrender yourself to your own desires, lest they graze away your strength like a bull.
They will strip off your leaves and eat your fruit, and leave you like a withered tree.
For a stubborn soul destroys its owner and makes him a source of joy to his enemies.
A pleasant mouth will multiply a person's friends, and the lips of the righteous offer greetings of peace.
Let those who greet you be many, but let your confidant be one in a thousand.
If you acquire a friend, acquire him through testing, and do not rush to trust him.
There is a friend who is a friend only for the moment and does not stand by you in a time of distress.
In your prosperity he is like you, but in your misfortune he distances himself from you.
If you fall, he will turn against you, go away from you, and hide.
Keep away from your enemy, and be cautious with your friend.
A true friend is a strong friend, and those who find him find a treasure.
A faithful friend has no price, and his goodness cannot be weighed.
A faithful friend is medicine for life, and one who fears God is such a friend.
Those who fear God will establish their friendships, for their friends will be like them, and their deeds will match their reputation.
My son, accept instruction from your youth, and you will find wisdom into your old age.
Approach her like a sower and a reaper, and gather her abundant produce. You will toil only a little, and soon you will eat her fruit.
How difficult wisdom is for fools! Those who lack understanding will not endure her.
She is like a heavy stone upon him; he will not wait, but will throw her away.
Her name accords with her teaching, and fools do not discern her.
Listen, my son, and accept my teaching; do not neglect my discipline.
Put your foot into her snare, and put your neck under her burden.
Put your shoulder under her and carry her, and do not be distressed by her burden.
Draw near to her with all your heart, and keep her ways with all your strength.
Examine, investigate, and seek, and you will find. Hold firmly to her and do not let her go.
In the end you will find rest and delights in her, and you will rejoice in her final reward.
Her snares will become a secure resting place for you.
She will clothe you in a garment of honor and bind a crown of praise upon you.
If you wish, my son, you will become wise; if you apply your heart, you will become discerning.
If you are willing to listen, you will learn; if you incline your ear, you will become wise.
Stand in the assembly of the elders. See who is wise and stay close to him.
Be eager to hear every account, and do not let the proverbs of the wise escape you.
See who is wise and seek him out; let your foot wear down his thresholds.
Consider the fear of God, and meditate on his commandments every day. He will set your paths straight and teach you what you have longed to know.
Do not do evil, and evil will not find you.
Keep away from evil, and it will keep away from you.
Do not sow in the plowed field of sin, lest you reap it sevenfold.
Do not ask God for authority or the king for a gift of honor.
Do not declare yourself innocent before God, and do not be foolish before the king.
Do not seek to become a judge unless you have the strength to put an end to injustice, lest you become afraid in the presence of a rich man and bring disgrace on your reverence for God.
Do not bring guilt upon yourself in the city's assembly, and do not embroil yourself in its lawsuits.
Do not repeat your sins, for you have not been acquitted of the earlier ones.
Do not say, “He takes account of my many offerings, and when I offer to the Most High, he accepts my offerings.”
Do not grow weary of the words of your prayer. Do not delay giving alms, and do not delay carrying out a commandment.
Do not laugh at someone who is suffering bitterly, for there is one who raises up and brings low.
Do not harbor evil thoughts against a brother, or against a friend or companion either.
Do not choose to tell any lie, because its outcome is not good.
Do not hide yourself in an assembly of rulers, and do not change the words of your prayer. Do not love yourself more than the people who are with you.
Remember that wrath does not pass away.
Humble yourself very deeply, because the end of all human beings is worms.
Do not exchange a friend for money, or a brother you have for the gold of Ophir.
Do not exchange a good and beautiful wife for pearls.
Do not mistreat a slave who works faithfully, or a hired worker who toils hard.
Love a wise slave as yourself, and do not withhold freedom from him.
Do you have livestock? Examine it, and if it is sound, keep it.
Do you have sons? Discipline them, and get wives for them while they are young.
Do you have daughters? Guard their bodies, and do not let your face beam at them.
Marry off a daughter, and trouble will go away; but give her to a wise man.
Do you have a wife? Do not leave her. But if she is wicked, do not trust her.
Honor your father with all your heart, and do not forget your mother who gave birth to you.
Remember that without them you would not exist. How will you repay them for raising you?
Fear God with all your heart, and honor his priests.
Honor your Creator with all your heart, and do not abandon his ministers.
Praise him and honor his priests as well. Give them their due, as you were commanded: the bread of offerings and the firstfruits of the hands.
Extend your hand to the poor as well, so that your blessings may be complete.
For a gift is an act of kindness in the eyes of all creatures. Do not withhold kindness even from the dead.
Do not stay away from a house of mourning, and mourn with all who mourn.
Do not be reluctant to visit the sick, because for these things you will be shown mercy.
In everything you do, remember the end, and you will never sin.
Do not contend with someone stronger than you, lest you fall into his hands.
Do not argue with someone who possesses gold, lest he outweigh you, for gold has destroyed many and leads even the hearts of kings astray.
Do not quarrel with a talkative man, and do not put wood on a fire.
Do not quarrel with a contemptible person, lest honorable people insult you.
Do not reproach someone who has repented of his sins. Remember that we are all sinners.
Do not laugh at someone who has grown old. Remember that some of us grow old.
Do not rejoice over someone who has died. Remember that we all die.
Do not neglect the accounts of the wise, and study their proverbs, for from them you will receive instruction for the time when you stand before rulers.
Do not grow impatient with the accounts of the elders, which they heard from their fathers, for from them you will receive instruction for the time when an answer is required.
Do not become a partner of a thoroughly wicked person, lest you be burned in the flame of his fire.
Do not confront an unjust person, lest he lie in ambush for you.
Do not lend to someone more powerful than you. If you do lend, consider it lost.
Do not guarantee a debt for someone more powerful than you. If you do guarantee it, consider yourself responsible for paying.
Do not sit in judgment with an unjust judge, lest you judge alongside him according to his wishes.
Do not travel with a headstrong man, lest he make your troubles worse, for he goes his own way, and you will perish through his foolishness.
Do not quarrel with an unjust man, and do not dispute with him in a deserted place, for your blood is of little value in his eyes, and if you have no one to rescue you, he will kill you.
Do not share a secret with a fool, because he cannot keep it hidden.
Do not reveal what is in your heart to everyone, lest he put you under an obligation for a favor.
Do not be jealous over your wife, lest she learn evil cunning against you.
Do not give yourself over to a woman, allowing her to rule over everything you have.
Do not associate with a prostitute, lest you fall into her traps.
Do not confide in a singing woman, lest she ruin you with her tales.
Do not gaze at a virgin, lest you become liable for twice her dowry.
Do not give yourself over to a prostitute, lest you lose your inherited property.
And you will be disgraced in the city streets and have your name entered in the [?] of debts.
Do not turn your gaze toward a beautiful woman, and do not contemplate beauty that is not yours, for many have perished through a woman's beauty, and love for her burns like fire.
Do not talk at length with another man's wife or prolong conversations with her, lest your heart turn aside to follow her and you go down to the realm of the dead guilty of bloodshed.
Do not abandon your old friend, for a new one is not his equal. A new friend is like new wine: when it has aged, you will drink it.
Do not envy a wicked person, because you do not know what his end will be.
Do not envy a wrongdoer who prospers. Remember that no one is vindicated until death.

Keep away from a person who has the authority to kill, and you will not live in fear of death. If you approach him, do not put your life at fault. Know that you are stepping among traps and walking over snares.
Answer your companion as well as you can, and share your confidence with the wise.
Share your thoughts with someone who fears God, and let all your conversations concern the ways of the Lord.
Let righteous people eat at your table, and let your boast be in the fear of God.
Through a judge’s wisdom a city is put in order, and one who rules over nations is wise and discerning.
A talkative man is feared in a village, and someone reckless in his speech is hated.
A wise judge teaches his people, and a wise ruler makes his town a place to live.
As the judge of a people is, so are his servants; as the head of a city is, so are its inhabitants.
An unjust king destroys his people, but a town flourishes through the wisdom of its rulers.
Authority over the world is in the Lord’s hands, and he appoints over it someone suited to the time.
Authority over everything is in the Lord’s hands, and he gives his honor to those who fear him.
In all your actions, do not wrong your friend, and do not walk in the way of the arrogant. Keep away from every sin and from falsehood, and do not walk with a haughty spirit.
For pride is hateful before God and human beings, and both detest robbery and oppression.
Kingship passes from one nation to another because of sins, pride, and wealth.
Why should dust and ashes be proud, when worms crawl in him even while he lives?
A physician cuts open his sides and his intestines. Today he walks about, and tomorrow he dies.
At a person’s death, maggots are his share, and his worm crawls before him.
The beginning of people’s sins is their pride, and their deeds lead their hearts astray.
For pride is the source of sin, and sexual immorality is the source of both. Therefore God singled out their afflictions and struck them with an utterly devastating blow.
The Lord overturned the throne of the proud and seated the humble in their place.
The Lord uprooted the root of the proud and planted the humble in their place.
The Lord uprooted the traces of the proud and erased their memory from the earth.
He destroyed them and uprooted them and uprooted them, and erased their memory from among humanity.
For pride was not allotted to human beings, nor arrogance of heart to those born of women.

Honorable offspring are what is sown among humans. Honorable offspring are those who fear God. Honorable offspring are those who keep the commandments. Dishonorable offspring are what is sown among humans. Dishonorable offspring are those who do not keep the commandments.
Among brothers, the elder is honored, but the one who fears God is honored more than he is.
A resident foreigner who is poor and distressed finds his glory in his fear of God.
It is not right to dishonor a righteous poor person, nor to honor a wicked rich person.
Honor the great man, the ruler, and the judge; but no one is greater than someone who honors one who fears God.
Free people will serve a wise slave, and an understanding person will not complain when disciplined.
Do not be lazy about doing your work, and do not put on airs when you are in need.
For someone who works and has money to spare is better than someone who puts on airs but lacks food.
My son, honor yourself with humility, and give yourself the consideration you deserve.
My son, if someone condemns himself, who will acquit him? Or who will honor someone who despises himself?
There is a poor person who is honored for his wisdom, and there is a rich person who is honored for his wealth.
Someone honored in poverty will be honored all the more in wealth, and someone despised in wealth will be despised all the more in poverty.
A poor person's wisdom will lift up his head and seat him among rulers.
Do not praise someone for being handsome, and do not criticize someone for being ugly.
For the bee is lowly among flying creatures, but what it produces is the choicest of all produce.
Do not laugh at someone dressed in patched clothing, and do not despise someone whose mouth tastes bitterness, because God's mysteries are extraordinary, and his works are hidden from human beings.
Many despised people have sat on a royal throne, and people whom no one would have imagined have worn robes of honor.
Many kings have been disgraced all at once, and honored people have had their honor diminished.
Do not enter a partnership before examining the matter. Investigate first, and then make an agreement.
Do not give an answer before you have listened, and do not speak in the middle of someone else's account.
If you have strength, do not quarrel, and do not multiply your acts of oppression amid injustice.
My son, do not let your troubles multiply. Whoever runs to increase them will not succeed. My son, if you do not run, you will not catch up, and if you do not seek, you will not find.
There is someone who runs, grows weary, and toils, yet falls behind in everything.
There is someone who toils and labors, whose body is weak, who lacks everything and is exceedingly poor. The Lord's word will show him favor and rescue him from the dust and ashes.
He raised his head and exalted him, and many will marvel at him.
Good and evil, life and death, rich and poor are equal before God.
Wisdom, modesty, and knowledge of the law come from the Lord. Love and the paths of good deeds come from him.
Error and darkness were created for sinners, and evil grows old with those who grow up in wickedness.
The Lord’s gift remains with those who fear him, and his will is established forever.
One person becomes rich out of his poverty, while another person’s wealth does not stay with him.
At the time when he says, “I have found rest for myself; now I will enjoy my good things,” he does not know what his end will be: he will leave them to others and die.
My son, stand firm on your path and rely on it; walk in its ways and grow old in its works.
Do not marvel at the deeds of the wicked. Instead, wait for the Lord and remain in his light, because it is easy for the Lord to make a poor person rich suddenly.
A day’s misery makes prosperity forgotten, and a person’s end will come upon him.
Do not praise anyone before you have examined him, for a person is praised at his end.
Do not let everyone into your house, for a deceitful person has many ambushes.

The heart of the proud is like a captive partridge in a cage, and like a lookout watching for someone's downfall. How numerous are the sins of the wicked! Like a dog that enters every house and snatches things away, so a wicked person enters every house and causes turmoil.
He turns good things into bad things, and uses desirable objects to set a trap.
A fire blazes from a little kindling; so a wicked person pours out blood like water.
Beware of an evil person, because he creates evil, lest you take on a lasting blemish.
Do not attach yourself to a wicked person, lest he corrupt your path and turn you away from your covenant.
If you do good to an evil person, you accomplish nothing, and there is no gratitude for your kindness.
Do good to a righteous person, and you will find repayment—if not from him, then from his Lord.
There is no benefit for anyone who honors an evil person, but whoever does good to a righteous person does not lose out.
He will bring twice as much harm upon you in your time of need. Do not give him your weapons, lest he use them to fight against you.
God too hates evil people, and brings his retribution upon the wicked.
Do good to a good person, and withhold from an evil person. Give to the humble, and withhold from the insolent.
A friend is not recognized in prosperity, and an enemy does not remain hidden in adversity.
For when a person prospers, his enemies are distressed, and in his adversity a friend withdraws.
Never trust an enemy, for he is like bronze whose rust stains it.

Even if he obeys you and walks humbly before you, take care to be wary of him. Be toward him like someone who reveals a secret, and he will not find a way to harm you; in the end you will learn his jealousy.

Do not place him beside you, so that he does not turn around and take your place. Do not seat him at your right hand, lest he seek your seat. In the end you will understand my words and marvel at what I have said.
For who will pity a snake charmer bitten by a snake? So too with anyone who approaches wild beasts.
So too, anyone who associates with an unjust man will not escape until fire burns within him.
As long as he goes along with you, he does not reveal himself to you; but if you fall, you cannot find his strength.
An enemy makes signals with his lips, while in his heart he devises a deep scheme. Even if tears flow from his eyes, if he finds an opportunity, he will not have his fill of your blood.
If misfortune strikes you, you will find him there like a man offering help, but he will seek to trip you up.
He shakes his head and waves his hand, whispers a great deal, and twists his face into a grimace.
Whoever approaches pitch gets it stuck to his hand, and whoever associates with an unjust man clothes himself in his ways.

Do not carry someone heavier than yourself, and do not associate with someone richer than yourself. What partnership can an earthenware pot have with a bronze cauldron? It strikes the pot and breaks it. Or what partnership can a rich person have with a poor person?
For a rich man sins and is unconcerned, while a poor man sins and prays.
If you are useful to him, he will put you to work; but if you become poor, he will abandon you.
If you have possessions, he will make his conversation with you pleasant. He will strip you bare and feel no concern.
While he carries out his own wishes with you, he will make you think that he is doing you a favor. He will deceive you and call you a capable man.
He will shame you with his schemes until he has his way with you. Once or twice he will overpower you; then, when he sees you, he will hide from you and shake his head at you.
Be careful not to fall into his hands, and do not be misled by his lack of understanding.
When a rich man approaches you, keep your distance from him, and he will continually draw you closer.
Do not draw too close, lest you be pushed away; and do not keep too far away, lest you be hated.
Do not be confident about speaking with him, and do not trust his many conversations, because his many conversations are tests. He will wear you out until he knows your ultimate intentions.
He exacts repayment without mercy and has no pity on the lives of many.
Take care and be watchful, for you are walking among robbers.
Every living creature loves its own kind, and a human being loves someone like himself.
Among all living creatures, a human being clings to his own, to his own kind.
What fellowship can a wolf have with a lamb? So it is with an unjust man and a righteous man.
How can a viper be at peace with a dog? Or how can a rich man be at peace with a poor man?
Wild donkeys in the wilderness are a lion’s food; likewise, the poor are the rich man’s pasture.
A rich man falls and is pushed into trouble; a poor man falls and is pushed from bad to worse.

A rich person speaks, and his supporters are many; they make even his offensive words sound good. A poor person speaks, and they tell him, “Be quiet!” Even if he says something good, they give him no opportunity.
A rich person speaks, and everyone listens; his admirers raise him to the clouds. A poor person speaks, and they say, “What did he say?” If he stumbles, they knock him down.
Wealth without sins is good, and poverty accompanied by sins is bad.
A person's heart changes their face, whether for good or for bad.
Radiant faces are the signs of a good heart, and abundant talk expresses the thoughts of sinners.
Blessed is the man whose mouth has not caused him to stumble, and from whose eyes judgment has not been hidden.
Blessed is the man whose own soul has not despised him, and whose efforts have not all come to nothing.
Wealth does not suit a small-minded person, nor does money suit a man with a grudging eye.
Whoever denies himself gathers for others, and a stranger will enjoy his goods.
If someone is bad to himself, to whom will he be good? He does not even enjoy his own goods.
No one is worse than someone who is bad to himself, and he receives an evil reward.
If he happens to do good, he does so by mistake, and in the end he will see his own wickedness.
In a fool’s eyes his portion is too small, and whoever takes what belongs to his neighbor destroys himself.
A grudging eye considers bread too much, and dry bread lies on the table.
If you have the means, my son, provide for yourself; and if you have the means, treat yourself well.
Remember that until now you have not seen death, and the decree of Sheol has not been revealed to you.
Before you die, do good to your friend, and give him whatever he asks of you.
Do not deprive yourself of the good of the day, and do not desire anything shameful.
For you will leave your possessions to others, and the fruit of your labor to those who cast lots.
Give and receive, nourish yourself, and do everything that is good to do before God.
For all human beings surely wear away, and the generations of the world surely die.
Like the leaves of trees, some of which fall while others sprout, so are the generations of flesh and blood: one generation dies, and another is born.
All his deeds are revealed before him, and the work of his hands follows after him.
Blessed is the man who meditates on wisdom and reflects with understanding,
who turns his heart toward her ways and considers her paths,
going out after her like a tracker and lying in wait along her paths.
He peers at her through the windows and listens at her doors.
He camps around her house and drives his tent pegs into her foundations.
He settles in a good campsite.
He lays his hands on her boughs and makes his home among her branches.
He sits in her shade away from the heat and shelters in her dwellings.
Whoever fears God will do this, and whoever learns the law will walk in her.
She will welcome him like a mother and draw him close like the wife of his youth.
She will feed him the bread of wisdom and give him the water of understanding to drink.
He will lean on her and not fall; he will trust in her and not be put to shame.
She will raise him above all his companions and open his mouth in the assembly.
She will fill him with joy and gladness and give him an everlasting name as his inheritance.
Sinners [?] will not walk in her, and wicked people will not see her.
She is far from the rebellious, and those who speak evil will not reach her.
It was not fitting in the mouths of the wicked, because it was not given to them by God.
Praise will be spoken in the mouths of the wise, and whoever has mastery of it will teach it.
Do not say, “It was because of God that I did wrong and sinned,” for he does not do what he hates.
Do not say, 'He made me stumble,' for he takes no pleasure in an unjust person.
He hates all evil and insolence, and he will not give them to those who love him.
God created human beings in the beginning and left them in the hands of their own inclination.
If you wish, you will keep his commandments, and if you trust in it, you too will live.
Fire and water are set before you; stretch out your hand toward whichever you wish.
For life and death have been given to human beings, so that they may choose life and leave death behind.
For God's wisdom is mighty, and he is powerful in mighty deeds.
His eyes see everything, and he knows all the thoughts of human beings.
He did not command human beings to sin, nor did he tell mortals to act wickedly, and he has no mercy on those who practice falsehood.
Do not long for a multitude of sinful children, and do not rejoice in any children of falsehood.
Even if they become numerous, do not rejoice in them, because they do not live in the fear of God.

Do not rely on their lives, and do not believe that they will have a good end, because one who [?] the will is better than a thousand, and someone who dies childless is better than someone who has many wicked children.
For through one person who fears God an entire town will be filled, but through a multitude of wicked people it will be laid waste.
My eye has seen many things like these, and my ear has heard things more terrible than these.
Fire burns in the assembly of the unjust, and wrath rules among a people who provoke anger.
He did not spare the ancient kings who filled the world with their might.
Nor did he have pity on the inhabitants of Lot's town, who acted wickedly because of their pride.
He did not have mercy on the accursed people, but decreed that they should perish because of their sins.
At that time six hundred thousand foot soldiers were cut down because of their grumbling.
Even if just one person stiffens his neck, it is a wonder if he escapes punishment, because mercy and anger are with him. He forgives abundantly, but he also calls sins to account.
As great as his mercy is, so too does he call sins to account, and he judges each person according to his deeds.
He will not let those who practice deceit and robbery escape, nor will he ever bring the hope of the righteous to nothing.
Everyone who practices righteousness has a reward, and each person receives from him according to his deeds.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart so that they would not know him, so that his works might be seen under heaven.
His mercy is visible to all his creatures, and he apportions his light and his darkness to human beings.
Do not say, “I will hide from the Lord. In the heights of heaven, who will remember me? Among so many people I will not be noticed. Or what is my soul among the spirits of all human beings?”
Look, heaven, the highest heavens, and the depths of the earth stand when he reveals himself over them.
The roots of the mountains and the foundations of the world tremble when he appears over them.
“Yet I will not take it to heart, and who will pay attention to my ways?
If I sin, no eye will see me. Or if I act deceitfully in complete secrecy, who will know?”
Those who lack understanding will say these things, and an unjust person will think this way.
Listen to me and accept my teaching, and give your attention to all my words.
I will speak my words with care and make my teaching known with wisdom.
When God created his works in the beginning, he allotted them their laws at their creation.
He assigned their tasks until the end, and their authority for all the generations of eternity. They neither hunger nor thirst, neither toil nor grow weary, and their strength does not diminish.
They do not hate one another, and they will never transgress his word.
After these things he looked upon the earth and blessed it with all its produce.
He filled its surface with the lives of all living creatures and gathered all their deeds within it.
God created Adam from the earth, and he will return him to it.
He allotted them a fixed number of days to live and gave them authority over everything.
In his wisdom he clothed them with strength and covered them with awe.
He put the fear of them upon all flesh, upon the animals and the birds.
He created for them a mouth, a tongue, eyes, and ears, and allotted them a heart to understand.
He filled their hearts with wisdom and understanding and taught them good and evil.
To show them the mighty deeds of his works, so that they might understand his wonders.
So that they might proclaim reverence for him throughout the world.
And praise his holy name.
He set a covenant before them and taught them the law of life.
He established an everlasting covenant with them and made his judgments known to them.
They saw his glorious splendor with their own eyes and heard his majestic words with their own ears.
He said to them, “Be careful, and do not lie,” and gave them commands concerning one another.
Their ways are revealed before him and never pass out of his sight.
He appointed rulers over all the nations, but Israel is the Lord’s own portion.
All their deeds shine before him like the sun, and all their thoughts are revealed to him.
Their offenses are not hidden from him, and the sins of all humanity are recorded before him.
The merit of all human beings is sealed and stored with him, and the kindness of all human beings is guarded before him like the pupil of an eye.
After these things he will reveal himself and repay them, bringing their offenses down upon their own heads.
But he grants repentance to those who turn back, and he will destroy all who harm the righteous.
Return to the Lord, and you will turn back from destruction. Turn away from sinning and do not provoke him to anger.
For what benefit does God receive from all those who have perished in the world, rather than from those who live and give him praise?
How abundant are the mercies of God, who forgives those who turn back to him!
For he is not like these among humans, nor is his thinking like human thinking.
When the sun passes out of the day, the day itself becomes dark. So it is with a person who does not restrain his impulses, because he is flesh and blood.
God judges the heavenly powers, and also human beings, who are dust and ashes.
The whole world is examined together.
And the Lord alone is righteous.
Who can recount his works?
Or who can number his mighty deeds?
When human beings reach the end, they are only beginning; and if they turn back, they will be astonished.
What are human beings? What is their loss, and what is their gain? What is their goodness, and what is their wickedness?
The number of a person's days, if he lives a long life, is a hundred years.
Like filling a waterskin from the sea, and like a grain of sand, a thousand years of this world do not amount to a single day in the world of the righteous.
Therefore he is patient with them and pours out his mercy upon them.
Because he knows that their end is miserable, he grants them abundant forgiveness.

A person's compassion extends to his own relatives, but God's compassion extends to all his works. He makes them wise, disciplines them, teaches them, and brings them back, like a good shepherd tending his flock.
Blessed are those who hope for his mercy and those who accept his judgments.
My son, do not hold back someone who does good to his neighbor, and do not look grudgingly at someone who gives.
For just as rain puts an end to scorching heat, so a word transforms a gift.
For there is a good word that is better than a gift, and both are found among worthy people.
For a fool insults before doing a kindness, and the gift of a wicked person brings tears to the eyes.
Before you fight, find yourself a helper, and before you become sick, find yourself a physician.
Pray before distress reaches you, and in the time of distress you will find it, and it will answer you.
Before you stumble, pray and plead, and before you sin, give alms.
Do not hold back from putting away your sins, and do not remain careless until trouble comes upon you. Do not delay turning back from your sins. Remember that death does not delay.
Before you make a vow, prepare to fulfill your vows, and do not be like someone who puts his Lord to the test. Do not go on committing sins, because you have not been cleared of the earlier ones.
Remember that wrath comes at the end of all sins, and in the time of distress it will not turn its face away from you.
Remember hunger in days of plenty, and poverty and hardship in days of wealth.
From morning to evening the circumstances change, and all these things are good in God's sight.
A wise man will take thought for all these things, and in days of wickedness he will not fear evil.
Everyone who is wise should teach wisdom, and those who know it should give thanks.
Those learned in instruction will themselves become wise and will understand fully the sayings of parables, the words of wisdom, and instruction for the soul.
My son, do not follow the demands of your soul, but restrain it from its desires.
For if you do what your soul desires, you are like someone who does what his enemy desires.
Do not delight in excessive luxuries, lest you become doubly poor.
Do not be poor, drunken, contemptible, and boastful when there is nothing in your purse.
A drunken worker will not become rich, and one who loves meat will inherit poverty.
Wine and women make the heart reckless, and whoever clings to a prostitute will perish.
A shameless soul will destroy its owner.
Whoever believes too quickly lacks understanding. Who will acquit someone who sins against himself?
Whoever rejoices in evil will meet his ruin.
Whoever repeats a report lacks understanding.
Never repeat a report, and no one will reproach you.
Do not lie about either a friend or an enemy. If you have sins, plead for forgiveness for them, and never slander anyone.
Otherwise, whoever hears you will hate you and consider you wicked.
Have you heard a report? Let it die in your heart. It is not an arrow that will pierce you and come out.
A fool suffers labor pains over a report, as a woman in childbirth suffers labor pains over her baby.
Like an arrow that strikes a man's [?], so is a report in a fool's belly.
Reprove your friend so that he does not do evil, and if he has done it, so that he does not do it again.
Reprove your neighbor so that he does not say it, and if he has said it, so that he does not repeat it.
Reprove your friend, because often slander is groundless. Do not let your heart believe every report.
For there is someone who sins without meaning it in his heart, and there is someone who stumbles, but not with his tongue.
Reprove the wicked man who has wronged many people, and do not believe everything he says.
Words of prophecy and all wisdom are the fear of the Lord.
The fear of God is itself wisdom.
There is no wise person who is evil, and no thinking of sinners that is discerning.
There is cunning that produces sins, and there is a fool who has few sins.
There is someone with little knowledge who escapes sins, and there is someone with greater knowledge who sins.
There is someone who is cunning and wants to lie, and acts crookedly to [?] justice.
There is someone who appears humble and broken in spirit, but inside his heart is full of deceit.
There is someone who lowers his face while planning evil, and where people do not know him, they call him righteous.
There is someone who refrains from sinning because he lacks the power, but if he can do harm, he does.
There is someone whom a man recognizes by the look of his face, and whom a wise man knows on meeting him.
A man's appearance reveals his deeds, and a person's footsteps testify about him.
There is poverty that is unbecoming, and there is someone who keeps silent and is wise.
There is no gratitude for someone who rebukes a wicked person.
And he boasts where he has no right to boast.
A eunuch longs to sleep with a virgin; such is the person who administers justice under compulsion.
There is someone who is considered wise when he keeps silent, and someone who is hated for his excessive talk.
There is someone who speaks where he ought not to speak.
A wise man waits for the right time, but a wicked and insolent man does not wait for the right time.
There is someone who is hated for his excessive talk, and the life of someone who acts arrogantly will be hated.

There are things that bring a person harm, and there are conversations that bring him loss. Just as you throw a stone at a bird and make it fly away, so you will lose the friendship of your true friend and will not find it again.
There is someone who borrows much as though it were little, and repays it sevenfold.
A fool’s gift is not worth it, because his eyes are set on repayment of seven for one.

He gives little and reproaches much; he opens his mouth, speaks evil, and refuses. Today he lends, and tomorrow he demands repayment, and his collection is an act of vengeance. People like this are hateful to God and to human beings.
Just as tail fat cannot be eaten without salt, so is a word that is not spoken at the right time.
A word stumbles in a fool's mouth because he does not say it at the right time.
There is someone who escapes sins because of his poverty. Who is this who has become righteous and rests comfortably on his wealth?
There is someone who destroys himself out of shame and comes to ruin through hiding his face.
There is someone who, out of shame, makes his friend rely on him and gains an enemy for nothing.
Lying is an evil thing among people, and it is abundant in a fool's mouth.
He longs to steal and also to lie, and both his ways will bring him shame.
For a lying person's end is a curse, and his shame will perish with him.
Someone full of wise proverbs will present himself as insignificant, and a wise man will exercise authority among rulers.
A gift and a bribe put the eyes to shame, shut the mouth, and put an end to rebuke.
Hidden wisdom and concealed treasure—what benefit is there in either of them?
A man who hides his foolishness is better than a man who hides his wisdom.
My son, be very careful to flee from sin. If you approach it, it will bite you. Falsehood is like a lion's teeth, and it destroys human lives.
A prostitute is a double-edged sword, and there is no cure for the wound it inflicts.
From morning until evening she destroys dwellings and uproots many palaces.
The poor man's prayer passes, as it were, from his mouth to God's ear, and rises before the Judge of all ages.
An unjust man hates correction, but whoever fears God repents from the heart.
A wise man can be recognized by the expression of his eyes, and he quickly discerns the unjust.
Someone who builds his house through the strength of his companions gathers stones for his wall.
Like a sandy slope under an old man's feet, so is the strength of the unjust in the face of fire.
The wicked man's path is a stumbling block to him, because its end is a deep pit.
Whoever keeps the law restrains his impulses, and whoever fears God will lack nothing.
A wise man's knowledge abounds like a spring of water, and his understanding is like living water.
The heart of a wicked person is like a broken cistern, and throughout his life he will not learn wisdom.
A wise person hears a wise person's saying, acknowledges it, and adds to it. A fool hears it, laughs at it, and throws it aside.
The wicked man's tales are like a heavy load on a journey, but everything the righteous man says is gracious.
A wise man's speech is sought in the assembly, and people take his words to heart.
Wisdom is like a prison to a fool, and knowledge is like a burning coal to the foolish.
Instruction is like a trap at a fool's feet and like a shackle on his right hand.
A fool raises his voice in laughter, but a wise man laughs quietly.
Wisdom is like a gold collar to a person of understanding and like a bracelet on his right hand.
A fool's feet hurry into a house, but a wise man lowers his face.
A fool peers through the doorway into a house, but it is honorable for a man to stand outside and speak.
It is foolish for a person to eavesdrop at a door, and a wise man finds its disgrace grievous.
The wicked man's mouth speaks with all his force, but a wise man speaks with measure.
A fool's mouth is his heart, but a wise man's mouth is in his heart.
When a fool curses someone who has not wronged him, he curses himself.
A wise man's soul is distressed over a fool, because he does not know what to say to him.
Like a foul-smelling stone lying in the street, whose smell everyone flees, so is a fool: everyone keeps away from him.
When a man goes out into the street and disgraces himself, everyone who sees him claps his hands.
A foolish son is a disgrace to his father, and a daughter is born to his loss.
A foolish woman brings shame on her father and mother, and she will be disgraced by both.
Like singing in a house of mourning is a story told at the wrong time. But discipline and instruction are wisdom at every time.
Someone who teaches a fool is like someone gluing together broken pieces of pottery, and like someone waking a sleeper from a deep sleep.
Someone who teaches a fool is like someone eating bread when he is not hungry. When you have finished speaking, he says to you, “What did you say?”

Weep for the dead person, because he has been deprived of light, and for the fool, because he has been deprived of wisdom. There is no need to weep for the dead person, who is at rest, for an evil life is worse than death.
Mourning for the dead lasts seven days, but mourning for a fool lasts all the days of his life.

Do not cultivate pleasant conversation with a fool, and do not travel on the road with a pig. Keep away from him so that he does not trouble you or soil you when he shakes himself. Keep away from him, and you will find rest, and he will not wear you out with his endless talk.
For he is much heavier than lead, and what is his name but “fool”?
Sand, salt, and a load of iron are easier to carry than living with a foolish man.
Like a wooden crossbeam secured in the foundations at the corners of a house, so is a heart made sensible by thoughtful counsel: no terror will shake it.
A heart made wise by its own thoughtful reflection is like carved decoration on ornamented walls.

A small pebble lying on a rock, being very light, cannot stand against the wind. Just as a linen garment and white wool cannot withstand a whirlwind, so a fool's heart is broken within him and cannot withstand distress.
A blow to the eye brings down tears, and a blow to the heart puts an end to friendship.
Do not turn against your friend, and if you do turn against him, do not suppose that you still have his friendship.
Even if you draw a sword against a friend, do not despair, for there is a way out.
If you open your mouth against your friend, do not be afraid, for reconciliation is possible. But insults, revealing a secret, and a treacherous blow destroy friendship.
Support your friend in his poverty, so that you may also share in his prosperity. Be his companion in his time of distress, so that you may also have a share in his gain.
Smoke rises before a fire, and an insult comes before bloodshed.
If your friend becomes poor, do not shame him, and do not hide yourself from him.
If your companion reveals a secret to you, do not disclose it, lest everyone who hears you be on guard against you and consider you untrustworthy.
Who, then, will set guards over my mouth and a seal of dignity upon my lips, so that I may speak no deceit with them and my tongue may not destroy me?
God, my Father and Lord of my life, do not make me stumble because of them.

Who, then, will set a whip over my thoughts and a rod of instruction over my heart, so that the Lord himself may have mercy on my sins, so that, when they gather, they may not take possession or delight in destruction?
So that my offenses may not multiply and my sins may not grow strong and expose me before my enemy, and so that the one who hates me may not rejoice over me.
God, my Father and Lord of my life, do not cast me into their error. Do not give me a proud look.
And remove a reckless heart from me; do not let anything good escape me.
Let the lust of the flesh not make me reckless, and let a shameless desire not rule over me.
Children, listen to the instruction of my mouth. Whoever takes heed will not be put to shame.
For the wicked person is caught by his speech, and the fool stumbles through his own mouth.
Do not accustom your mouth to oaths, and do not sit in a court of law.
For everyone who swears many oaths will not escape blows. Likewise, anyone who lies and swears an oath will not escape guilt.

A man who swears oaths accumulates guilt, and strife will not depart from his house. If he swears mistakenly, the sin rests on him. Even if he speaks truthfully, he should not swear, because constantly swearing is hateful, and he will not be innocent.
Even if there is another thing comparable to it, let it not be found in Jacob's inheritance. Whoever restrains himself from these things will live and will not become entangled in sins.
Do not train your mouth in foolishness either, for it too contains lying words.

Remember that you have a father and mother, and what terror you will escape, so that you do not stumble before them and disgrace yourself by what you have learned, and say, “If only I had not been created,” and curse the day on which you were born.
For a man who learns idle words will not learn wisdom all his life. A man who acts recklessly, dishonoring his own body, does not accept instruction.
My soul hates two kinds of people, and a third stirs up anger: a man who acts recklessly, dishonoring his own body, will not rest until fire burns within him.
To the flesh of a lustful man, all flesh is sweet, and he will not stop until he perishes.
A man who is unfaithful on his marriage bed says to himself, “Who sees me? Look, the walls of my house hide me, and the roof of my house shelters me. No one sees me. Who can stop me from sinning?”
He does not know that God's eyes are ten thousand times greater than the sun. He sees the paths of all human beings and perceives their deeds in the deepest darkness.
For before anything comes into being, it is revealed before him, and even after the end of the world, he will judge it.
Where a person does not expect to be caught, this man will be exposed in the streets of the city.
So too with a woman who wrongs her husband and produces an heir by another man.
First, she has been false to God's law; second, to the husband of her youth; and third, through sexual immorality and adultery, she has borne a child by a stranger.
She too will leave the assembly, and her sins will be remembered against her children.
Her children will not take root in the earth, and her branches will not bear fruit.
Her memory will remain as a curse, and her sins will not be erased.
All the inhabitants of the earth will know, and all who remain in the world will understand, that nothing is better than the fear of God, and nothing is sweeter than keeping his commandments.
Wisdom will praise herself and will be honored among God's people.
In God's assembly she will open her mouth, and among his hosts she will be praised.
I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, and like a mist I covered the earth.
I pitched my tent in the lofty heights, and my throne was among pillars of cloud.
In heaven I dwelt together with him, and I walked in the depths of the abysses.
At the springs of water and at the foundations of the world, and among all peoples and nations, I held dominion.
Among all these I sought rest for myself, to settle where I might prosper.
Then the Lord of all commanded me, and he who made me and pitched my tent said to me, “Dwell in Jacob and become firmly established in Israel.”
Before the ages I was created, and my memory will never cease, forever and ever.
In the holy tent I served before him, and so I became established in Zion.
In the city he loves as he loves me, I found rest, and in Jerusalem was my dominion.
I grew among an honored people, in the Lord’s portion, and within his inheritance, Israel.
Like a cedar I grew in Lebanon, and like an oil-bearing tree on Senir, the snowy mountain.
I grew tall like a palm tree in En-gedi and like a rosebush in Jericho. I grew like an olive tree in the plain, and I grew tall like a plane tree beside the water.
Like cinnamon and the fragrance of spices, and like fine myrrh, I made my scent sweet. Like frankincense, galbanum, onycha, and balsam, and like fine oil, I gave off my fragrance.
Like an oleander I put down my roots, and my branches were branches of praise and honor.
Like a vine I was lovely in my beauty, and my shoots were shoots of radiance and splendor.
Turn toward me, all who desire me, and delight yourselves in my good produce.
For my teaching is sweeter than honey, and to those who inherit me, sweeter than the honeycomb.
Those who eat me will hunger for me again, and those who drink me will thirst for me again.
Whoever listens to me will not fall, and none of his deeds will be ruined.
All these things are written in the book of the Lord's covenant. The law that Moses commanded us is an inheritance for the congregation of Jacob.
It is full of wisdom like the River Pishon, and like the Tigris in its harvest season.
It overflows with understanding like the Euphrates, and like the Jordan in the days of Nisan.
It pours out teaching like a river, and like the Gihon in the days of the grape harvest.
The first will not exhaust wisdom, and the last will not fully grasp it.
For wisdom has grown greater than the great sea, and thought greater than the great deep.
I too am like a river that irrigates, and like a water channel flowing down to gardens.
I said, “I will water my garden and drench my garden beds.” And look, it became a torrent for me, and my river reached the sea.
Again I will speak my teaching in the morning, and I will leave it for many generations.
Again I will speak my teaching in prophecy, and its end will be far away.
My soul has desired three things, and they are beautiful before God and before human beings: harmony among brothers, affection among friends, and a husband and wife living in agreement.
My soul hates three kinds of people, and their lives distress me greatly: an arrogant poor man, a lying rich man, and a foolish old man who lacks understanding.
You did not gather wisdom in your youth; how will you find it in your old age?
How fitting sound judgment is for the elderly, and understanding for those advanced in years!
How fitting wisdom is for great men, and discernment and insight for the honored!
The honor of elders is their depth of understanding, and the fear of God is their glory.
I have praised nine things that did not enter my mind, and ten that I have not spoken of: a man who rejoices in his latter days will, while still alive, see the downfall of his enemies.

Happy is the husband of a good wife, who has not drawn a plow with an ox and a donkey together. Happy is the man whose tongue has not brought him trouble and who has not served someone inferior to himself.
Happy is the man who has found mercy and speaks to an ear that listens. Happy is the man whom poverty has not broken and whom affliction has not broken.
The fear of God is exalted above all these things.
The beginning of the fear of the Lord is to love him, and the beginning of faithfulness is to follow him. Hold on to it, my children, and do not let it go, because there is nothing like it.
No wound is like a wound of the heart, and no wickedness is like the wickedness of a woman.
No distress is like the distress caused by someone who hates you, and no retribution is like the retribution of an enemy.
No venom is more bitter than a snake's venom, and no hostility is more bitter than a woman's.
It is better to live beside a lion or a dragon than to live in a house with an evil wife.
The wickedness of a wicked wife makes her husband's face pale and blackens it like the color of sackcloth.
The husband of a foolish woman sits among his companions and sighs despite himself.
Even great evil is nothing like a little of a woman's wickedness. May the lot of sinners fall upon her!
Like a sandy slope beneath an old man's feet is a sharp-tongued wife to a gentle husband.
Do not be enticed by an evil woman's beauty, and even if she has property, do not desire her.
For a wife who mistreats her husband is hard labor and bitter disgrace.
And the heart of the man who is with her is covered in darkness. An evil wife is a wound to the heart. A wife who does not honor and praise her husband weakens his hands and makes his knees buckle.
Sins began with a woman, and because of her we all die.
Do not give water an outlet, or an evil wife freedom and authority. For just as a breach letting out water keeps widening, so an evil wife keeps going and sinning.
If she will not follow you, cut off your flesh, give it to her, and send her away from your house.
Happy is the husband of a good wife, for the days of his life are doubled.
A capable wife makes her husband happy, and he will complete the years of his life in joy.
A good wife will be given to a man who fears the Lord as a reward for his good deeds.
Whether rich or poor, his heart is always happy, and his face is radiant.
At three things my heart trembled, and at four I was greatly afraid: the grumbling of an assembly in a crowd of people,
and the blow of a tongue—all of them together.
An evil wife is a harsh yoke, and whoever bears it grasps a scorpion.
A drunken wife is a great source of anger; she is reckless and does not conceal her disgrace.
A woman's promiscuity can be recognized by her raised eyes and her eyelids.
Set many guards over a shameless woman, because she has no rest unless she steals.
Hurry after a woman with shameless eyes, and do not delay, lest she deceive you.

Like a thirsty traveler coming in from the road, whose mouth is open for cold water and who drinks from every source, she leans against every tree and opens her quiver to every arrow. Such is an adulterous woman, whose womb is open to every man.
A good wife is a gift from the Lord, and there is no price for restraint of appetite.
A modest wife is grace upon grace, and no weight can measure restraint of speech.
Like the sun rising in the expanse of heaven is the beauty of a good wife in the dwelling of her household.
Like a lamp shining on the holy lampstand is a woman's beauty as she stands in her house.
Like golden beads on a silver column, her heels are beautiful in her well-ordered house.
My son, be careful in your youth, and do not give your strength to strangers.
Seek your portion from all the land, a good plain in which to sow your seed, confident in your offspring.
Thus will your crops be, and your family will not be just anywhere.
An adulterous woman is to be regarded as nothing, but another man's wife is to be regarded as a tower of death to those who attach themselves to her.
A wicked wife will be given as the lot of an unjust man, but a righteous wife will be given to the man who fears the Lord.
Disgrace will wear down a shameless woman, but a modest daughter will keep herself hidden even from her husband.
A shameless woman will be regarded as a dog, but a woman who fears the Lord has modesty.

A wife who honors her husband will be considered wise by everyone, but a wicked wife who dishonors him in her arrogance will become known to everyone. As for a good wife, blessed is her husband, for the years of his life are doubled. A wife's quarreling brings humiliation, and she will seem like a lingering fever.
A loud and talkative wife is like a horn sounding the alarm for battle. The soul of any man who has all these things will be thrown into the turmoil of battle, and his life will be spent in distress.

My heart is broken over two things, and over a third I am deeply grieved: a freeborn man who has become poor and needy; people of renown who have been stripped of their honor; and someone who turns away from the fear of God to do wrong—hand him over to the day of slaughter.
A merchant escapes sin only with great difficulty; rather, he stumbles in one thing after another. A shopkeeper is not free from sin.
Many have sinned because they have no fear, and whoever wishes to multiply sins is careless with his eyes.
A peg goes in between one stone and another, and sins are wedged between buyer and seller.
My son, if you disregard the fear of God, you will lose much in a short time.
As thick smoke rises above a fire, so people's talk rises above their reasoning.
Just as the cultivation of a tree produces fruit, so people's reasoning is based on their thoughts.
If you seek truth, you will find it and wear it like a splendid robe.
A bird of the sky settles with its own kind, and truth goes to those who practice it.
A lion lies in wait to destroy; so does wickedness lie in wait for those who commit sins.
The talk of the wise is always wise, but a fool changes like the moon.
Among fools, watch for the right time; among the wise, speak continually.
The talk of fools is hateful, and their laughter is insolence.
When they laugh, stop your ears.
One who sheds blood listens to the words of the unjust. Do not sit among the wicked.
Whoever reveals a secret loses his trustworthiness and will not find a friend who is like his own self.
Test your companion and rely on him, but if he reveals a secret entrusted to him, do not follow him.
For just like a man who has lost his share, you have lost your friend's friendship.
You have let him fly from your hand like a bird, and you will not catch him.
Do not pursue him, because he has escaped like a gazelle from a snare and like a bird from a trap.
For a wound can be bandaged, and a quarrel can be reconciled, but whoever reveals a secret has cut off hope.
Whoever winks his eye will meet his downfall.
I have hated many, but none like him; God too will hate him and curse him.
Whoever throws a stone will have it return upon him, and whoever strikes in secret will be handed over to destruction.
Whoever digs a pit will fill it with his own body, and whoever sets traps will be caught in them.
Whoever devises evil will fall into it, and he will not know where the evil that comes upon him comes from.
These snares and traps are for those familiar with them, and they will accompany them until the day of their death.
Jealousy and anger are also unclean, and a deceitful man ruins his own way.
He will meet with retribution from God, because all his sins are carefully preserved against him.
Let go of what is in your heart, and then pray, and all your sins will be forgiven.
One person holds on to anger against another; how can he seek healing from God?
He himself is human and is unwilling to forgive another. Who will forgive his sins?
Remember death and put aside hostility. Remember Sheol and destruction, and refrain from sinning.
Remember the commandment, and do not hate your neighbor before God. Give him what he lacks.
Keep away from quarrels, and sins will keep away from you.
For an unjust person who loves disputes sows hostility between brothers.

Whatever you throw into the fire will burn, and the more you prolong a dispute, the more it grows. A person's anger matches the glory of his deeds, and his pride rises with the abundance of his possessions.
Resin and pitch kindle a fire, and many disputes cause bloodshed.
If you blow on a fire, it will burn; if you sprinkle water on it, it will go out. Both come from you.
May the slanderous tongue also be cursed, for it has caused many killings.
A slanderous tongue has led many into captivity and scattered them from nation to nation. It has driven even the honored citizens of cities from their homes and utterly destroyed the houses of kings.
The slanderous tongue has led many into captivity and separated them from their possessions.
A blow from a rod makes a wound, but a blow from the tongue breaks bones.
Many have been killed by the sword, but not as many as have been killed by the tongue.
Blessed is the man who has escaped it and has not become entangled in its fury. Blessed is the man who has not pulled under its yoke and has not been bound in its chains.
For its yoke is a harsh yoke, and its chains are chains of iron.
The death it brings is an evil death, and rest in Sheol is better than being with it.
It will not burn among the righteous, and sparks of fire will not burn you.
All who abandon the fear of God will fall into it. Fire will burn among them and will not be extinguished. It will overpower them like a lion and tear them apart like a leopard.
You put a seal on your silver and gold.
And weigh your words.
Be careful not to fall, so that you are not thrown down before your enemy.
The one who lends to his neighbor establishes good bonds [?], and the one who takes him by the hand keeps the commandment.
Lend to your neighbor in his time of need, and reassure your neighbor; at the appointed time, keep your word.
Keep your word and stand by your friend, and you will always get what you need from him.
For many borrowers have sought a loan and provoked their lenders.

When he borrows, he kisses the lender's hand and raises his voice in praise of his neighbor's possessions. But when it is time to repay the loan, he gives himself a respite and puts it off for a long time.

If the lender manages to recover half, he considers it a lucky find. His hands come away empty of his possessions, and he gains an enemy. Moreover, the borrower repays him with quarrels and insults for no reason, and with disgrace instead of honor.
Many have stopped lending, not out of wickedness, but because they fear needless trouble.
Nevertheless, be patient with the poor; be patient with them.
Give them relief, as one keeping the commandment, and if there is a loss, do not let it trouble your mind.
Lose your money for your brother and your friend, and do not put it beneath a stone or a wall.
Store up treasure for yourself through righteousness and love, and it will be better for you than everything you possess.
Gather up charitable giving and put it in your treasury, and it will rescue you from everything evil.
It will be strong defenses, a spear, and a wall for battle, and it will give you security against many.
A good man is one who guarantees his friend’s debt, but someone who has lost all shame runs away from his guarantor.
An evildoer disregards the kindness of his guarantor.
And whoever abandons his Creator abandons his deliverer.

Guaranteeing debts has ruined many, and they have abandoned their possessions like the waves of the sea. It has stripped even wealthy people of everything, and they have gone away to a foreign nation.

A sinner who transgresses the Lord's commandments falls into guaranteeing debts, and whoever is eager to take sins upon himself falls under judgment. Guaranteeing debts brings many sins: a person is oppressed for nothing and faces judgment.
Guarantee your friend’s debt according to your ability, and save yourself from a double burden.
The essentials of human life are bread, water, clothing, and a house that covers one’s nakedness.
For the life of a poor person under the shelter of roof beams is better than great wealth while living as a stranger.
Whether he has much or little, no one knows, and no one sees what he does inside his house.
It is a miserable life to go from house to house, unable to open one’s mouth in important disputes.
You are a stranger and drink in humiliation, and after all this you will hear bitter words.
“You are a stranger! Come in, set the table, and eat whatever you have in your hands.”
“Make way for someone honored, for a guest has put me under pressure.”
It is to God that you are lending, and he will repay you sevenfold.
A man who loves his son will keep whipping him, so that he may rejoice in the end.
Whoever disciplines his son will rejoice in him and boast about him among his companions.
Whoever teaches his son makes his enemy jealous and boasts about him before his friends.
His father died, and [?] that he had not died, because he left someone like himself behind.
During his lifetime he saw him and rejoiced, and at his death he was not grieved.
He repays his friends with kindness and exacts repayment from his enemies.
Whoever pampers his son will have many wounds, and his heart will tremble at every cry.
Like a spirited horse that has not been broken in, so is a rebellious son who does not obey his father.
Discipline your son so that you are not mocked; if you laugh with him, he will torment you.
Do not go along with his wishes, lest he provoke you and in the end set your teeth on edge.
Do not give him authority in his youth, and do not overlook all his offenses.
Bow his head while he is a child, and strike his loins while he is small, lest he grow strong and rebel against you.
Take pains to teach your son and be strict with him, lest he cause you to stumble through his foolishness.
For a poor man who is alive and physically sound is better off than a rich man whose body is afflicted.
I have loved a sound life more than gold, and a good spirit more than pearls.
There is no wealth like bodily health, and no joy like a cheerful heart.
It is better to die than to live a miserable life, and to descend to Sheol than to suffer lasting pain.
Good things kept covered over a closed mouth are like food placed on graves.
What enjoyment do the idols of the nations have, since they neither eat nor drink nor smell? So it is with someone who has wealth but does not use it.
He looks with his eyes and sighs, like a eunuch who lies beside a virgin while his master holds him accountable.
Do not give yourself over to sorrow, and do not bring yourself down through your own counsel.
For gladness of heart is a person’s life, and a person’s disposition prolongs his life.
Comfort yourself and refresh your heart, and put sorrow far from you, because grief has killed many, and sorrow has destroyed them.
Jealousy and anger wear away one's days, and worry brings gray hair before its time. A cheerful heart has a hearty appetite, and everything a person eats nourishes his body.
Sleeplessness wastes away a rich man's flesh, and anxiety interrupts his sleep.
Worry about food drives away slumber, and severe illness interrupts sleep.
A rich man labors to gather possessions for himself, and when he rests, he enjoys luxuries.
A poor man labors to meet the needs of his livelihood, and if he rests, he will be in need.
Whoever loves money will not remain innocent, and whoever pursues possessions will go astray through them.
For many became rich and trusted in their possessions, but those possessions could not save them from disaster or rescue them on the day of their end.
For wealth is a stumbling block to fools, and everyone who goes astray through it stumbles.
Blessed is the rich man who is found blameless and has not gone astray in pursuit of wealth.
Who is he? Let us praise him, for he has done many mighty deeds among his people.
Who is this who held fast to it and had peace, and for whom it became a source of praise? Who is this who could have gone astray but did not, and could have harmed his neighbor but did not?
Therefore his prosperity will grow strong, and assemblies will recount his praises.
My son, if you sit at a rich man's table, do not open your throat greedily over it, and do not say, “There is not enough for me.”
For God hates a grudging eye, and he has created nothing worse than it. That is why the eye trembles before anything else and sheds tears down the face.
Do not reach out your hand for whatever you see, and do not crowd your hand into the dish.
Recognize that your neighbor is like yourself.
Eat what is set before you like a proper man, and do not be a glutton, so that you will not be hated.
Take care to behave properly.
When you sit among many people to eat, do not reach out your hand before they do.
For a little is enough for a righteous man, and he will not be restless on his bed.
Pain, sleeplessness, exhaustion, torment, and an upset stomach accompany a greedy man. A man who lives moderately enjoys sound sleep: he sleeps until morning, and his mind is at ease.
If you are distressed by the food, withdraw from the midst of the gathering, and you will find relief.
Listen, my son, and do not despise me; in the end you will understand my words. Be humble in everything you do, and no evil will come near you.
A generous eye is blessed over its bread, and good testimony about it is trustworthy.
Do not show off your strength with wine either, for aged wine has destroyed many.
For just as a furnace tests the work of a metalworker, so wine incites wrongdoing.
Wine is like living water to a person who drinks it in due measure. What is life for someone who lacks wine? For it was created from the beginning to bring joy.
Wine drunk in due measure brings joy to the heart, delight, and good times.
Wine drunk amid quarreling brings pain, poverty, and a headache.
Too much wine becomes a stumbling block to a fool; his strength diminishes and his wounds multiply.
Do not rebuke your friend at a drinking party, or distress him while he is enjoying himself. Do not speak to him about his shortcomings, or quarrel with him in front of other people.
If they put you in charge, do not become proud, and do not take your place at the head of the rich. Be like one of them and attend to their needs; afterward, take your place.
Provide for all their needs, and then recline at table. Because of this, you too will rejoice when they are finished, and you will receive honor at the table.
Where wine is being drunk, do not tell stories, and do not show off your wisdom all the time.
Like a seal on a purse of gold, so is the praise of God at a wine banquet.
