Like a gold necklace, signet rings, and emeralds, so are fine words at a wine banquet.
Do not exalt yourself among rulers, and do not seek to insult those older than you.
Do not talk too much at the table, and leave for home while you still have your senses.
Do what you wish in the fear of God, and not to your own harm.
And for all these things, bless the name of God, who has satisfied you with his good gifts.
Whoever seeks to serve God will receive instruction, and when he prays before him, God will answer him.
Those who fear God will gain wisdom through his judgments, and they will bring forth abundant wisdom from their hearts.
A crafty person conceals instruction and follows a path of his own choosing.
A wise person does not leave wisdom hidden, but a wicked person does not guard his tongue.
Do nothing without advice, and after you have acted, you will not regret it.
Do not walk on a dark road, lest you stumble over a stone twice.
Do not trust the path of the wicked.
And be careful in your ways.
In everything you do, guard yourself, for everyone who does this is keeping the commandment.
Whoever guards his way keeps God's commandment, and whoever trusts in God will never perish.
No evil will befall someone who fears God except as a trial, and he will turn back and escape.
The heart of a wicked person is like a swiftly turning wheel, and all his thoughts are like a pig.
The friends of a wicked person are like a horse ready to be ridden, which neighs beneath anyone who loves it.
Why is one day in the year different from another, since all the heavenly lights serve the days of the year?
Yet they were distinguished by God's wisdom, and he made appointed times and seasons from them.
Some of them he blessed and made holy, and others he made ordinary numbered days.
All human beings, too, were made from clay, and Adam was created from dust.
But in God's wisdom he distinguished them and made them inhabitants of the earth.
Some he blessed and exalted; some he made holy and brought close to himself; and some he cursed, overthrew, and uprooted from their homes.
Like clay kneaded in a potter's hand, so is a human being in the hand of his Creator, to establish him in all his works.
Good was created to stand opposite evil, life was created to stand opposite death, and darkness was created to stand opposite light.
Thus God displayed all his works in pairs, one opposite the other.
I too came last, like someone gleaning a vineyard after the grape pickers.
Through God's blessings I took my stand, and like a grape picker I filled my winepress.
Listen to me, rulers of the people; leaders of the assembly, pay attention to me.
Do not give your possessions to others, only to turn around and ask them for them.
While you are alive and have breath in you, do not give anyone power over you.
For it is better for your children to ask you than for you to ask them.
In all your dealings, retain the upper hand, and do not bring a blemish on your honor.
When the number of your days is complete, on the day of your death, leave your possessions to your children.
A saddle, a whip, and a load for a donkey; discipline, bread, and work for a slave.
Do not give him rest. If you let him hold his head high, he will seek his freedom.
Put your slave to work so that he does not rebel.
For idleness produces many evils.
Give him responsibility in your house as is appropriate for him. If he does not obey you, increase his fetters. But do not treat everyone this way, and do nothing contrary to the law.
If you have only one slave, treat him as yourself, for losing him is like losing yourself. If you have only one slave, regard him as your brother, and do not fight against your own flesh and blood.
For if you mistreat him, he will leave and disappear.
And in which direction will you find him?
Whoever seeks emptiness finds falsehood, and a dream is an empty joy.
Like someone grasping a shadow and chasing a bird, so is anyone who believes a vision of the night.
A vision and a dream of the night are like this: the likeness of a face opposite a face.
And from the head of his people [?] came victory; or who is the liar who will prevail?
All omens, divinations, and dreams are delusion, and whoever believes in them has his heart set on them.
Even if going astray in the thoughts of the night was decreed by God, do not set your heart on them.
For many have lost their way through dreams and stumbled on their paths.
In a place where there are no sins, God is the shepherd, for the wisdom of the wicked is believed at night.
A wise man examines many things, and a diligent person investigates everything.
Someone without experience knows little.
But someone with experience has increased his wisdom.
I saw much as I gained experience, and many things happened to me.
Many times I came close to death, but I escaped because of those experiences.
The Lord fulfills the wishes of those who fear him.
For his hope is great, and he delivers.
Blessed is the spirit of the person who fears God.
On whom did he rely, and who became his support?

The Lord’s eyes are on all his servants. He shields and rescues them. He is a great source of confidence, a shelter from an enemy, a deliverer from an adversary, a rescuer from injury, and a support against falling.
Joy of heart, light for the eyes, health in life, and blessings—all these will come doubly upon the righteous.
The burnt offerings of the wicked are offerings of injustice.
And their offerings are not accepted.
For God takes no pleasure in the burnt offerings of sinners, nor does he forgive them because of their many offerings.
Someone who presents an offering from what belongs to the poor is like someone who slaughters a son before his father.
The bread of charity is the life of the poor, and whoever withholds it from them sheds innocent blood.
Whoever kills his neighbor inherits his possessions.
Whoever sheds innocent blood robs God. Whoever withholds a hired worker’s wages wrongs his Creator, and he will receive an evil repayment.
One builds and another tears down. What have they gained except fruitless labor?
One blesses and another curses. To which of the two voices will God listen?
If someone washes after contact with a corpse and then touches it again, what has he gained from his washing?
If someone fasts from his sins but then goes back and commits them again, who will hear his prayer? What has he gained by fasting?
If you do what is written in the Law, you increase your service.
And whoever keeps the commandment—blessed is his soul!
The one who presents an offering lays down good [?].
And whoever practices righteousness keeps the law.
God’s will is that you turn away from everything evil. Restrain your strength so that you do not do what is hateful.
Do not appear before him empty-handed.
For everyone who does what is good is keeping the commandment.
The offerings of the righteous are the prayers of their mouths, and their deeds pierce the heavens.
The gift of a good person will be accepted, and the memory of the righteous will never be forgotten.
Give generously to the poor, and do not hesitate over your gifts.
Let your face shine whenever you give, and lend joyfully to someone who will not repay you.
Give to God as he has given to you, with a generous heart and an open hand. For whoever gives to the poor lends to God; who can repay except him?
For God is the one who repays, and he will repay you ten thousand times ten thousand.
Do not offer a bribe, because he will not accept it.
Do not rely on offerings taken by robbery, for God administers justice, and there is no partiality before him.
The prayer of the poor comes before him, and he hears the plea of those whose spirits are distressed.
He does not disregard the groaning of orphans, and he hears the prayer of widows.
He hears the bitter anguish of the poor person’s soul, and their prayer bends the clouds down.
The prayer of the poor rises above the clouds and enters the presence of the Lord of majesty. It does not pass away until he examines it
and passes a just judgment. The Lord will not disregard it, abandon it, or cease until he calls the might of the wicked to account.
He will repay the nations until he destroys the strength of sinners and completely cuts off unjust rulers.
until he brings back upon the wicked the harm they have done, and upon evildoers their own schemes,
until he judges his people’s case and makes them rejoice in his repayment,
and puts their enemies to shame in a time of distress, like a rain cloud when it is needed.
Save us, God, all of us!
And bring your wrath upon the nations that do not know you.
Raise your hand against the foreign people, and let them know your might.
Just as you showed your holiness through us before their eyes, so show your holiness through them before our eyes.
Let them know, as we know, that there is no God besides you.
Renew signs and perform wonders anew.
Strengthen your hand and your right arm.
Stir up anger and pour out wrath.
Break the enemy and put an end to the adversary.
Bring on the end and make the appointed time arrive, for there is no one who can say to you, “What are you doing?”
In anger and fire destroy the enemy and all the great men and rulers of the nations.
Destroy the crown of the enemy who says, “There is no one like me.”
Gather all the tribes of Jacob,
and let them inherit, as you said in ancient days.
And rejoice over your people, who are called by your name, over Israel, whom you called your firstborn.
Have mercy on your holy city, on Jerusalem, the place where you dwell.
Fill Zion with your majesty and your temple with your glory.
Confirm the testimony of your deeds as in the beginning, and let the prophecies of your prophets, who speak in your name, come true.
Give a reward to whoever waits for you, and let your prophets be found trustworthy.
Hear the prayer of your servants according to the desire of your people, so that everyone at the ends of the earth may know that you alone are God forever and ever.
The appetite accepts every food, but some food is more pleasant than other food.
The mouth tastes the flavor of food, and the heart of the wise discerns the words of the wicked.
A secretive heart has many cares, and a wise man understands these things.
A woman’s beauty adorns her face, and she surpasses everything the eyes desire.
As the first of your possessions, acquire a good wife, for she is a helper like you and a pillar supporting you.
Where there are no fences, vineyards are grazed bare; and where there is no wife, a man wanders and is scattered.
For who will trust a bandit who is like a gazelle, leaping from town to town? So it is with a man who has no wife: he will die wherever he happens to be.
And he says to his friend, “I love you.” Yet there is a friend who is a friend in name,
who does not last until death. Let a true friend be like your own self to you.
Why were hateful and wicked people created, except to fill the earth with deeds of injustice?
A bad friend draws near to the table, but in a time of distress he stands at a distance.
A friend who fights against the enemy and holds a shield is good.
Do not praise your friend in his presence, and do not give him authority in your house.
Examine every adviser; yet there is advice that is sound.
Guard yourself against a wicked adviser, and first find out what he wants, for he too is thinking of his own interests. Be careful that he does not ensnare you with malicious deceit.
and say, “How good your path is!” Then he will stand opposite you and watch your disgrace.
Do not consult someone who hates you, and keep your secret hidden from him.

Do not take counsel with a woman, lest you commit adultery with her; or with an enemy, lest you fight; or with a merchant about his trade; or with a seller about his sale; or with an unjust man about doing what is right; or with someone who has no compassion about showing compassion; or with a hired worker who is dishonest in his work. Do not share a secret with an unjust hired worker, and do not act as adviser to a slave who wants to defraud his master.

Keep company with righteous people, who fear sinning before God and whose hearts are in tune with yours. If such a person harms you, he harms himself; and if he does good to you, he does good to himself.
For his faithfulness will keep him alive, and he too is faithful like you.
A person's heart will rejoice in his way more than in worldly wealth that brings no benefit.
And in all these things, keep praying to God that he may set your path straight in truth before other people and before everything.
The Lord created everything: good and evil, life and death. Whoever controls his tongue will be delivered from evil.
Everyone who is wise in his own mind is a fool.
For there is someone who is wise but is hated for his talk, and he deprives himself of all honor.
And there is a wise person who is wise for himself, and the fruits of his deeds can be seen in his face.
There is a wise person who is wise at all times, and the fruits of the wise are for themselves.
The person who is wise for himself will have his fill of delights, and everyone who sees him will praise him.
The wise person among the people will inherit honor, and his name will endure forever.
My son, test yourself during your life, and see what is bad for you; do not give it to yourself.
For not all food is good, and not everyone is satisfied with a little.
Do not give yourself too much rich food, and do not look with envy at an abundance of food.
For illness comes from too much food, and whoever eats too much becomes sick.
For many have died because of too much food, but whoever is careful prolongs his life.
Honor the physician before you need him, for God created him too.
A physician receives wisdom from God and gifts from the king.
Because of the physician’s understanding, they will exalt him and set him before kings.
God created medicines from the earth, and a wise person will not despise them.
For bitter water was made sweet through wood, so that God’s power might be known.
He gave human beings wisdom so that they might glory in his mighty deeds.
With these the physician gives relief from pain.
The perfumer also prepares remedies with medicines, so that work and wisdom may not disappear from the face of the earth.
My son, even in your illness pray before God, for he is the one who heals.
Put away wrongdoing and falsehood, and cleanse your heart of every sin.
Give the physician room as well, because there is benefit in him too.
For there is a time when healing succeeds through his hands.
Let him pray before God, so that health may be restored through his hands, and healing and life may come through his hands.
For whoever sins before God is handed over to the physician.
My son, shed many tears over the dead. Grieve and speak a lament. Gather up his body as is fitting for him, and do not neglect his burial.
Wine and food for the people who dance. Observe mourning as he deserves, for a day or two, for the sake of other people, and be comforted for the sake of the living.
For distress is born of sorrow, and a troubled heart crushes more than death does.
In worry for the poor [?] and brings distress, for the life of the poor is a curse to the heart.
Do not set your heart on oaths. Remember distress and put away sins.
Do not rely on wealth, because there is no hope in it. Like a bird of the sky that flies and settles, so is wealth among people: it makes you happy and makes someone else miserable.
Remember that this sentence applies to you: yesterday for him, and today for you.
As the dead person has come to rest, put the memory of him to rest, and take comfort at the departure of his soul.
The scribe’s wisdom will increase his wisdom, and the person who does not deal with worthless things will become wise.
For how can someone who holds the plow blade become wise, who drives oxen and [?] with oxen, and whose conversation is about young bulls?
His mind dwells on the furrow for his seed, and he stays awake to finish his work.
Likewise, all the craftsmen are busy together. Night and day they ponder these things: the work of engraving, seals, and pearls. Their thoughts, too, are needed for the work of their craft.

To sit at the furnace and examine the weighing tools: the flames of the fire blister his flesh, and he burns in the heat of the fire. He lowers his hand according to his understanding, and his eyes are fixed on the design of his work.
Likewise, the potter sits at the wheel and moves the vessel with his foot. His eyes are on the vessels throughout all his work.
His arms break up the clay, and before he dies he is bent and stooped. His heart is set on finishing his work, and his sleepless hours are spent building his kiln.
All these concern themselves with their success, and each becomes wise in the work of his craft.
Without them a city cannot be inhabited, and wherever they live they will not go hungry. Yet they will not sit in the council of the people.

They will not be raised to prominence in the assembly or sit on the judge’s seat. They will not understand covenants and judgments. They will not grasp the teaching of wisdom or understand the proverbs of the wise.
For they are skilled in the world's work, and their thoughts are on the work of their craft.
But the one who devotes himself to fearing God and understanding the law of life—
he will seek wisdom like that of all the ancients and turn to the prophets of old.
He will learn the accounts of all the people of the world and reflect on profound matters.
He will learn the wisdom of proverbs and gain understanding of all hidden things.
He will walk among rulers and serve among kings and nobles. He will travel through the cities of the world; he will conceal good and evil among people.
He will set his heart on praying and ask God for mercy. He will open his mouth in prayer and ask for favor concerning his sins.
He will become wise through the spirit of understanding. He will bring forth proverbs, one or two, and people will praise him for his thoughts.
He will understand the proverbs of the wise and gain understanding of hidden things.
He will bring forth instruction in wisdom and glory in the law of life.
Many will learn from his wisdom, and his name will never be forgotten. His memory will never disappear, and his name will not be forgotten from generation to generation.
Assemblies will recount his wisdom, and the people will proclaim his praises.
If he wishes, he will be praised among a thousand; and if he remains silent, among a small people.
Understand, and I will speak: my teaching is like the moon on the twelfth day.
Listen to me, you righteous people, and let your flesh blossom like lilies and like cedars planted beside water. Let your fragrance be sweet like fine spices.
Like the fragrance of Lebanon with its cedars, and like the root of the royal lily, raise your voices and praise together. Give thanks to God for all his works.
Recount his might with praises and thanksgiving and with a loud voice, and speak this way:
All the works of God are beautiful together, and all were created for their purposes.

Let no one say, “What is this for, and what is that for?” For all things were made with a purpose. Let no one say, “This is bad, and that is good,” for all things are governed at their proper time. At his command the sun rises, and at his command he makes it set.
His will is carried out with joy, and no one delays his command.
The deeds of all flesh are before him, and no one hides from his presence.
Nothing is small or great before him, and nothing is strong or difficult for him.
His blessing flows like a river, and like a river it waters the worlds.
Likewise, in his anger he judges the nations and turns their irrigated land into salt.
The paths of the righteous are straight before him, but for the wicked those same paths turn aside.
Good things were created from the beginning for the good, and also for the wicked, whether for good or for evil.
The chief necessities for human life are water, fire, iron, salt, fat, wheat, milk, honey, grapes, wine, oil, coverings, and clothing.
All these things benefit the good, but for the wicked they turn into a curse.
There are winds created for punishment. In their fury they uproot mountains, and in the time of wrath they display their strength and appease the spirit of the one who created them.
Fire, hail, and deadly stones—all these were created for judgment.
Beasts with fangs, scorpions, snakes, and the sword of punishment are for destroying the wicked.
When he commands them, they rejoice, and throughout all their days they do not disobey his word.
For they were created from the beginning. Understand, human beings, that all these things are written in the book.
All his works are good, and everything was created for its own time.
Let no one say, “This is worse than that,” for all of them are gathered in the storehouse and are governed at their appointed time.
Now bless God with all your heart, and praise his name.
God created great things, and harsh conditions for human beings, from the day they come out of their mother’s womb until they rest upon the land of the living.
Their glory, the thoughts of their hearts, and the outcome of their words, until the day of their death.
From those who sit on royal thrones to those who sit in dust and ashes;
from those who put on a crown to those who wear the clothing of poverty:
Anger, jealousy, sorrow, fear, dread of death, strife, and misfortune—and when they rest on their beds, it disturbs them in their sleep at night.
He is ruled by a vision of the night, like a man fleeing from a pursuer.
If there is a desire in his heart, he wakes up and sees that he has nothing.
With all flesh, their anxiety remains with them, and wealth drives away their sleep.
Everything that is from the earth returns to the earth, and what is from above returns above.
Everyone who sins and lies will perish, but the upright of the world will endure.
Fraudulent wealth will be swept away like a torrent, like rivers filled by a passing cloud.
When they are stripped bare, they will come to an end.
The offspring of wicked people will not endure, for the root of sinners is like an ear of grain that grows on the edge of a cliff.
and like bindweed growing on the edge of a channel, which dries up before all other greenery.
The deeds of the upright will be blessed in their time, and the deeds of the righteous will endure forever. Whoever draws near to them is like someone who finds treasure.
Greatness and honor establish a name, but better than both is someone who has found wisdom.
Building and planting renew a name, but better than both is a good wife.
Old wine gladdens the heart, but better than it is the affection of a friend.
The flute and harp make music sweet, but better than both is a pure tongue.
Grace and beauty delight the eyes, but better than both are ears of grain in a field.
A friend and a companion will be blessed in due time, but better than both is a wise wife.
A brother and a helper are there in a time of distress, but charitable giving delivers more than either.
Gold and silver make one's footing secure, but better than both is good advice.

Strength and power lift the heart, but the fear of God surpasses them both. There is no lack in the fear of God, and with it there is no need to seek a helper. The fear of God has been exalted above everything. Hold on to it, my son, and do not let it go, because there is nothing like it.
The fear of God is blessed in due time, and it is praised above every honor.
My son, do not refuse anyone who asks you. Do not be good at killing, but be good at giving life.
Let no one consider a man who depends on other people’s tables to be alive. Whoever loves delicacies hates his own life, and to a man who understands, these things are a pain in the bowels.
A shameless person's request tastes sweet in his mouth, but it burns like fire within him.
O death, how bitter you are to a rich man who lives comfortably on his possessions, a man who is strong and always prosperous and still has the strength to enjoy luxuries!
O death, how welcome you are to a man who is broken and dispirited, an old man who is always stumbling, who lacks money and has no strength to work!
Do not fear death, because it is your allotted portion. Remember that those who came before and those who come after share it with you.
For this is the end of all human beings before God.
The offspring of the unjust are a despised seed, and the offspring of sinners are a family to be pitied.
Power will perish from an unjust son, and deprivation will dwell with his descendants.
The upright children of an unjust father will curse him, because on his account they were despised in the world.
Woe to unjust people, for sorrow accompanies them until the day of their death!
A woman who bears children is a joy to her people. If an unjust father dies, his righteous children will not mourn for him.
For the wicked person's end is destruction, but the name of those who do good will never be forgotten.
How does he return to you the deposit you give him?
A daughter is a heavy burden on her father, and worry about her drives away his sleep: in her youth, lest she be defiled, and when she has a husband, lest she be hated.
In her virginity, that she may not be disgraced; and concerning her husband, lest she go astray in her mind and follow another man.

My son, keep watch over your daughter, lest she give you a bad name and make you the subject of gossip and grumbling among the people, and shame you in your village assembly through the people's gossip. Do not let her go out from the place where she lives, or wander from house to house.
Do not reveal what is in your heart to everyone, and do not embellish stories among women.
For just as a moth attacks clothing, so a woman’s jealousy comes from her companion’s wickedness.
Remember now the works of God. I will recount what I have seen. His works were created by his word, for all his creatures carry out his will.
Like the sun that shines on everything, the Lord’s mercies are revealed over all his works.
The Lord's holy ones cannot fully recount the mighty deeds of his wonders. He has given strength to those who love him to stand before his glory.
He searches the deep and the heart, and all human thoughts are as clear as the sun before him, because nothing is hidden from God.
Everything that comes into the world is revealed before him, both what has passed and what is still to come. All hidden things are revealed before him.
No wisdom escapes him, and no mystery of power is concealed from him.
Wisdom stands before him forever.
He establishes all his works forever in truth, and all of them are praised in holiness.
They live and endure forever. They are all ready to carry out all his wishes, and they act with great speed in their appointed duties.
They are all in pairs, one opposite another, and he did not create any of them without a purpose.
Rather, each is paired with another. Who can have enough of seeing their glory?
He made the sun to be seen and praised, a wondrous instrument, the work of the Most High.
At midday it scorches the earth, and who can withstand its heat?
The sun burns the mountains, three times hotter than a furnace fanned for a smith's work. Its blaze is like fiery vapor; it sends out its shining rays and dazzles the eyes.
Great is the Lord who made it, and at the Holy One’s words it hastens on its course.
The moon also appears at its appointed time, an indication of the seasons and a sign from ancient times.
For from the moon come the signs of festivals, a light that comes to its end.
The moon is true to its name and grows splendidly through its changes, an instrument of the heavenly army shining in the firmament of heaven.
The beauty of heaven and the glory of the stars.
At the Holy One’s words they stand according to their appointed order, and they do not deviate from their courses.
I too will praise men of kindness, our ancestors who lived in their generations.
He will bestow great honor on them, and all their greatness will last through the generations of the world.
They revealed signs through their prophecy.
And kings in their understanding, wise men who taught through their wisdom, and rulers who made proclamations in their songs of praise,
By means of lyres and harps, and speakers of proverbs in the writings of powerful men,
And [?] in strength, and at ease in their prosperity.
All these had honor in their generations, and praise in their own days.
Some of them left a name behind, so that their praises could be recounted.
And some of them have no remembrance, and they passed away as they passed away.
But these were men of kindness and righteousness; their kindness will not come to an end.
Their blessing endures with their descendants, and their root with their children's children.
Their descendants stand firm in their covenant, and their grandchildren in good deeds.
Their memory endures forever, and their honor will not be forgotten.
Their bodies were gathered to rest in peace, and their name lives from generation to generation.
And the people will recount their praises.

Noah was found righteous and blameless in his generation. At the time of the flood he became a substitute for the world, and through him deliverance came. God swore to him that there would never again be a flood.
The oaths that he swore to him in truth were that he would not destroy all flesh.
Abraham was the father of multitudes of nations, and no stain was put on his honor.
He carried out the commands of the Most High and entered into a covenant with him. The covenant was established for him in his flesh, and when tested he was found faithful.

Therefore God solemnly swore to him that all the nations of the earth would be blessed through his descendants, that he would multiply his descendants like the sand of the sea, and that he would set his descendants above all nations, giving them an inheritance from sea to sea and from the Euphrates to the ends of the earth.
He also swore to Isaac because of Abraham his father.

The blessing of all who came before rests on the head of Israel, whom he called, “Israel, my firstborn son.” He gave him an inheritance and established him as father of the tribes. He went forth and was divided into twelve tribes. Righteous men came from him, and he found favor in the eyes of all the living.
And Moses was beloved before God and also in the eyes of human beings; his memory is a blessing.
He made him great with blessings and gave him power to inspire awe.
He set him before the king, appointed him over the people, showed him his glory, and let him hear his voice.
Because of his faithfulness and humility, he chose him from all humanity.
He brought him near to his thick cloud and set before him the law of life and blessing, to teach his laws to the house of Israel, and his covenant and judgments to Jacob.
And he raised up a holy man like him, Aaron, from the tribe of Levi.
He made him a firm support for the people, bestowed on him some of his honor and glory, and chose him in the height of his honor.
He clothed him in blue garments and honored him with mighty vestments.

Moses laid his hand on him and anointed him with holy oil. This became an everlasting covenant for him and his descendants, for as long as the days of heaven, to minister and to bless his people in his name.
He chose him from among all the living to offer burnt offerings, sacrifices, and incense, and to make atonement for all Israel.
He gave him commandments and authority over covenants and judgments.
Outsiders opposed him and were jealous of him in the wilderness: the men of Dathan and Abiram, and the assembly of Korah in their strength.
God saw and became angry. He burned them with fire, brought a plague upon them, and destroyed them in the force of his anger.
He bestowed honor on Aaron and gave him his inheritance: the first portions of the holy offerings and the rows of bread, for him and his descendants.
But they received no inheritance in their land and shared no portion with them, because the Lord is his portion and inheritance among the house of Israel.

Phinehas son of Eleazar also received three honors through his courage, because of the zeal he showed against the Midianite woman and the Israelite man, and because he stood in the breach for the people and interceded for Israel.
Therefore God solemnly swore to him that he would establish an altar for him, and that the high priesthood would belong to him and his descendants forever.
David son of Jesse also inherited the royal inheritance for himself alone, but Aaron's inheritance belonged to him and his descendants.
Now bless God, who gave you wisdom of heart to judge his people in his name, so that their prosperity and their authority may not be forgotten throughout all generations forever.

Joshua son of Nun, a mighty warrior, was preserved through prophecy to become like the great Moses, to bring deliverance through his hand to those who loved him, to exact vengeance on hostile men, and to give the Israelites the promised land as their inheritance.
How splendid he was when he raised the spear in his hand and brandished it against the city!
Who could stand before him? For he fought the Lord's battle.
For through him the sun stood still, and one day became two days.
For he prayed before the Lord, who answered him and gave him strength. He answered him with hailstones and brought sulfur down from heaven.
He struck the hostile people and destroyed them all. All the nations doomed to destruction knew that God himself had fought against them, and Joshua himself followed God faithfully.
In the days of Moses, he and Caleb son of Jephunneh acted loyally by standing in the breach for the people, turning the assembly back, and putting an end to the bad report about the promised land.
They alone out of six hundred thousand were spared, to enter their inheritance, the land flowing with milk and honey.
He gave Caleb strength and remained with him until his old age, enabling him to take control of the strongholds of the land. His descendants too would inherit an estate.
This was so that Jacob's descendants would know that he fulfilled God's law and judgments.
Each one by name—all whose hearts did not go astray and who did not turn away from God's law—may their memory be a blessing.
May their bones blossom like lilies, and may they leave a good name to their children and their praises to all the people.

Loved by his Creator was Samuel, the judge and priest, who was asked for and was a Nazirite from his mother's womb, a prophet. Through his word the kingdom was established, and he anointed rulers and kings for the people.
By his law he gave commands to the assemblies, as the Lord of Jacob commanded.
He too crushed the enemies on every side of him when he offered a suckling lamb.
The Lord thundered from heaven and made his voice heard with a mighty crash.
He crushed all the rulers of Tyre and destroyed all the tyrants of the Philistines.
When he lay resting on his bed, he testified before the Lord and before his anointed one that he had taken no bribe or gift from anyone, and no one testified against him.
After his death he was consulted and showed the king his course. He raised his voice from the earth in prophecy to put an end to sins.
After him Nathan the prophet arose to speak before David.
For just as the fat is lifted from the holy offering, so David was lifted up from Israel.
He killed lions as though they were young goats, and wolves as though they were lambs.
In his youth he killed the giant and removed his people's disgrace. He swung his hand with the sling and shattered all Goliath's arrogance.
For he prayed before God, who gave him strength to kill the giant skilled in warfare, to exalt the power of his people Israel.
For this reason women praised him with tens of thousands. He fought swiftly.
He crushed the enemies on every side of him and took vengeance on the Philistines. He broke their power, and it remains broken to this day.
For this reason he raised his voice with words of thanksgiving and honor, and with all his heart he loved his Creator.
Every day he regularly recited his praises before the altar.
He offered great praises year after year.
God also forgave his sins, exalted his power forever, and gave him a royal throne over Israel forever.
After him a mighty king arose.
Solomon lived in peace, and God gave him rest on every side, so that he might build a house for his name forever.
How wise you were in your youth, Solomon! Through your understanding you made wisdom overflow like a river.
At the height of royal glory, your fame reached distant islands, and they longed to hear you.
Through the interpretation of wise proverbs in writing and through prophecy, you amazed the nations.
You were called by the name of God, to whom belongs the glory of having his name invoked over Israel. You gathered gold like lead and silver like dust.
You gave your strength to women and gave them power over your body.
You put a blemish on your honor and disgraced your bed, bringing guilt upon your descendants, so that they would groan on their beds.
and be divided into two kingdoms, with a pagan kingdom from the house of Ephraim.

Yet God did not abandon his kindness. He will not let his words fall to the ground, nor will he destroy the descendants of those who love him. He will not wipe out the children of his righteous ones. He will give deliverance to Jacob and a great kingdom to David.

Solomon died, and his son arose after him: Rehoboam, full of folly and lacking wisdom, who led his people according to his own thinking. May Jeroboam son of Nebat have no memorial: he sinned and caused Israel to sin, and placed a stumbling block before the house of Ephraim.
causing them to be exiled from their land. He greatly multiplied their sins.
He plotted every kind of evil,
until a prophet arose who was like fire, and whose word burned like a blazing furnace.
He brought famine upon them and tore them apart in his zeal.
By the word of the Lord he shut up the heavens and three times brought fire down from heaven upon the altar and upon wicked men.
How awesome you are, Elijah! Who is like you, worthy of such praise?
You raised a dead man from Sheol according to the Lord’s will.
You brought down nobles from their thrones.
In his trial he made their rebuke heard.
He anointed kings to bring destruction, and a prophet to succeed him.
He was snatched up in a whirlwind, on fiery horses, into heaven.
He is destined to come before the day of the Lord comes, to turn children back to their fathers and to bring good news to the tribes of Jacob.
Blessed is the one who saw you and died! Yet he will not die, but will surely live.

Elijah was gathered into the storehouses of heaven, and Elisha received a double portion of prophecy. His mouth spoke of many trials and signs. Throughout his days he did not tremble before anyone, and no mortal had power over him.
No word was hidden from him.
During his life he did extraordinary things, and in his death he raised a dead man.

Despite all these things, the people did not repent or turn away from their evil deeds, until they were exiled from their land and scattered throughout all the countries. Judah alone remained, a small realm belonging to the house of David.
Some of them repented, while others added to their sins.
Hezekiah built the city and brought water into it.
In his days Sennacherib came up against them and sent the Rabshakeh against them. He raised his hand against Zion and arrogantly blasphemed God.
Hezekiah spread out his hands before the Lord, and God quickly heard his prayer and delivered them through Isaiah the prophet.
He shattered the Assyrian army and struck them with a great blow.
For Hezekiah did what was good and walked in the ways of David, as Isaiah the prophet, renowned among the prophets, had commanded him.
For through him the sun stood still, and the king’s life was extended.
With a spirit of might he saw the things to come and comforted the mourners of Zion.
While he was in the world, he saw signs and trials before they came.
The name of Josiah is like a censer of incense mixed with an abundance of spices. His memory is sweet as honey to the palate and like a song at a drinking feast.
For he kept himself hidden from temptations and put an end to childish deeds.
He gave his heart wholly to God, and in days of sin he practiced righteousness.
Except for David, Hezekiah, and Josiah alone, they all acted corruptly. The kings of the house of Judah abandoned the law, right to the end.
They gave their strength to others and their glory to a foreign people.
And they uprooted the holy city and laid all its ruins waste in the days of Jeremiah,
who was a prophet from his mother's womb.
Ezekiel revealed the form of the chariot and saw a vision.
And he also said of Job that all his ways were righteous.
And the twelve prophets—may their bones shine beneath them, for they healed Israel and assured them that they would be delivered.
How shall we praise Zerubbabel, who was like a signet ring on the right hand?
And Joshua son of Jozadak also: in their poverty they erected an altar and built the holy temple, destined for everlasting glory.
May Nehemiah's memory grow great, for he restored our ruins, rebuilt our demolished places, and made our gates and bars.
Few were created on earth like Enoch.
And no mother gave birth to anyone like Joseph, and his body too was gathered in peace.
Seth, Shem, and Enosh were created among humankind, but above all these is the glory of Adam.
The greatest of his brothers and the crown of his people was Simon son of Nethaniah, the high priest. In his days the house was built and the temple strengthened.
And a wall was erected [?], and the courtyard was built.
And he dug a spring.
And he rescued his people from enemies.
How splendid he was when he came out of the temple, when he appeared from beneath the curtain!
Like the morning star among the clouds, and like the moon in the days of Nisan,
and like the sun shining upon palaces, and like a rainbow in the clouds,
And like ears of grain in a field, like a royal lily beside springs of water, and like the trees of Lebanon at harvesttime.
And like the fragrance of frankincense on a censer, and like a golden bowl beautifully worked and adorned with precious stones.
and like a splendid olive tree whose branches are great, and like an oil tree that provides sustenance through its boughs.
When he put on the holy garments and wrapped himself in garments of honor, when he came out to receive praises in the beauty of the sanctuary’s splendor.
When he received the portions of meat from his brothers’ hands, he stood above the rows, and his brothers surrounded him like a crown.
All the sons of Aaron, in their splendor, held offerings in their hands before all the people of Israel,
until he finished ministering at the altar and serving in holy joy.
He stretched out his hand toward the cup, took aged wine, and poured it out beside the altar as a pleasing fragrance.
Then the sons of Aaron sounded the horns before all the people of Israel. They made a mighty sound, offering blessing before all the people.
And all the people together fell face down on the ground to worship God.
They raised their voices in thanksgiving and rejoiced together in prayer.
And the people of the land praised God,
who did wonderful things on earth, who created human beings from their mothers’ wombs and guides them according to his will,
to give them wisdom of heart, so that there may be peace among them.
May steadfast love remain with Simon and with his descendants for as long as the heavens endure.
My soul was distressed by two nations, and the third is no nation.
The inhabitants of Gebal, the Philistines, and the foolish people who live in Shechem.
Every proverb of the wise and their riddles are written in this book.
Blessed is the man who meditates on these things, learns them, understands them, and puts them into practice.
The greatness of the fear of the Lord is exalted above everything. Look to it, my son, and do not abandon it.
I will give thanks to you, Lord and King, and praise your name, Lord, every day, and proclaim your name in songs of praise.
My hope from of old, Most High, you rescued my life from death and kept my flesh from destruction. You rescued my feet from the power of Sheol.
In your abundant mercy you rescued me. You saved me from stumbling and destruction. You rescued me from the hand of the one seeking my life and saved me from my many troubles.
and from the flame of fire that surrounded me.
My soul reached Sheol, and my spirit drew near to death.
I turned around to find help and looked for someone to support me, but there was no one.
I remembered the Lord’s mercies and his kindnesses from of old: he saves all who trust in him and rescues them from those stronger than they are.
I raised my voice from the earth and prayed.
I called to my Father on high: “Lord, mighty one and Savior, do not abandon me on the day of crushing distress.
I will praise your name at all times and remember you in songs of praise.” Then the Lord heard my voice and listened to my plea.
He saved me from every evil and rescued me from every distress. Therefore I will give thanks and sing praise and bless his holy name.
I was a boy, and I delighted in it and sought it.
My foot walked in truth, my Lord, and from my youth I knew instruction.
I prayed for it when I was young, and I found much instruction.
Its yoke became an honor to me, and I will give thanks to my teacher.
I resolved to do good, and I will not turn back when I find it.

My soul clung to it, and I will not turn my face away from it. I devoted myself to pursuing it, and I will never, ever forget it. My hand opened its door; I turned toward it and gained understanding of it.
In purity I found it, and I gained understanding from the beginning. Therefore I will not abandon it.
My inward parts burn like an oven to examine it closely. Therefore I acquired it as a good possession.
My Lord gave my tongue a reward, and with my lips I will praise him.
Turn toward me, you who lack understanding, and lodge in the house of learning.
How long will you lack these things and your soul remain so thirsty?
I opened my mouth and spoke with it: Acquire wisdom for yourselves without money.
Put your necks under her yoke, and let your souls receive instruction. She is near to anyone who seeks her, and whoever devotes himself to her finds her.
See with your own eyes that I labored little over it and gained much of it.
Listen to my teaching, brief as it is, and through me you will acquire silver and gold.
Let your soul rejoice in my repentance, and do not be ashamed of my praise.

Do your work before its appointed time, and your reward will be given at its appointed time. Blessed be God forever, and praised be his name from generation to generation. The book of Ben Sira is finished.
